title: Time-Zone Overlap: The Hidden Productivity Multiplier
excerpt: Why shared working hours matter more than hourly rates when you compare staffing options.

author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

When companies compare staffing options, they usually compare hourly rates. The number that matters more is how many hours your teams can actually talk to each other.

The Cost of Waiting

Blocked tickets

Every unanswered question parks a ticket. With a twelve-hour offset, a single clarification can cost a full day; three of them cost a sprint.

Review latency

Pull requests that wait overnight for review go stale, conflict with other changes and need rework.

Measuring Overlap

  • Count shared working hours per day, per team pair.
  • Track median time-to-first-response on questions.
  • Track pull-request cycle time before and after a staffing change.

Conclusion

A slightly higher rate with six hours of overlap is almost always cheaper than a lower rate with none. Measure the waiting, not just the hourly cost.
